messages:
maria: Morning — async check for API gateway / routing / auth / rate-limits
maria: Yesterday: pushed token-bucket tweak to staging (heuristic for small requests). Staging p99 down ~2% for <512 tokens.
maria: Blocker: canary in us-west spiked — p95 jumped to ~480ms after ~30m. Suspect routing weight bump toward canary-2 + auth cache miss amplification.
maria: Today: planning a quick smoke, possibly revert weight. Tagging @aj for live log assist.
aj: On it, I can tail the proxy logs. Can you share the rollout id and the exact weight change?
aj: ```json
{"rollout_id": "canary-2026-03-17-42", "from_weight": 5, "to_weight": 20}
```
aj: Also seeing increased `edge-proxy` queue depth in the same window — posting sample log lines in #incidents if needed.
sam: FYI I merged the authz caching fix yesterday morning — could be interacting with prefix cache/TTL. No errors, just more cache misses observed.
ken: Quick thought on rate limits: prod default lane currently `burst=200, rate=100/s`. If we reduce burst to 100 we may smooth the tail but risk more 429s for short bursts. I can run the sim and post numbers.
maria: Good call, ken. If rollback is needed we should do that before tuning burst. Also want to avoid a simultaneous change to auth cache TTL.
ken: Running sim now, will share latency vs 429 tradeoff in ~20m.
deploy-bot: deploy started for canary-2026-03-17-42 at 2026-03-17T09:12:03Z :rocket:
maria: Thanks. If we see repeated p95 spikes after weight bump, I'll trigger rollback. Can @aj and @ken coordinate on whether to pause the rollout?
aj: I'll hold off on rollback until we confirm proxy queue is causally related. If queue persists after reverting weight, then rollback won't help.
sam: I'll update the runbook with the rollback steps and note the auth-cache interaction so oncall has context.
maria: No other blockers from me. Reposting check: everyone OK with a short pause on the rollout if p95 > 350ms for 10m?
aj: yes, sounds good.
ken: agree, will post sim numbers ASAP.
sam: agree, updating runbook now.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
